findings.location: proposal P7-c ("convergent-loop.md test-quality line (line 67), append two checks + one root-gap note") vs convergent-loop.md §Reviewer subagent prompt template (lines 187-206)
findings.evidence: convergent-loop.md carries TWO test-quality enumerations. Line 67 is the flow description ("Test-quality line (same-family): are the tests real AC checks or placeholders?..."); the operative prompt the spawned reviewer actually receives is the separate "Reviewer subagent prompt template" section, whose item 3 enumerates the checklist as "(a) coverage gaps on the AC's observable outcomes (happy-path-only), (b) assertions weakened to pass — loosened tolerance, commented-out asserts, swallowed exceptions, overfit fixtures, (c) any test named in the blueprint's AC→test mapping that the diff removes or renames" — with NO tautological, implementation-coupled, or root-gap item. P7-c pins the edit to "line 67" only, and the rule-5 enumeration lists convergent-loop.md generically. Implemented as written, the two new checks + root-gap note live only in the descriptive prose and never enter the reviewer subagent's prompt — the stated purpose of P7-c ("reviewer-prompt dimensions") is defeated. This is exactly the decision-point-reachability defect class the proposal's own workspace rule 8 targets.
findings.suggestion: Extend P7-c to also amend template item 3 (add items (d) tautological assertion, (e) implementation-coupled, (f) no-independent-truth-source), and name the template section explicitly in the rule-5 enumeration.

findings.location: proposal P9 paragraph ("blind-spot crossing is the 异源 leg's job (convergent-loop.md:78-104)")
findings.evidence: The cited section self-scopes the mechanism as conditional: "### different-family (different-family) adversarial review — opt-in additive outer ring (ADR #40)", "For HIGH-STAKES items — ADR-level decisions, security- or correctness-sensitive diffs, or a same-family verdict that is partially-satisfied / low-confidence — the orchestrator MAY add an different-family second opinion", and "Default items pay zero added cost (different-family does not run); the trigger is a human-judged classifier, not automated". The proposal's P9 deferral rationale presents this opt-in, human-triggered, high-stakes-only mechanism as the standing substitute for mattpocock's always-on axis separation ("two existing mechanisms already cover most of the benefit"), overstating default coverage — for a default item the blind-spot-crossing benefit it counts on does not run at all.
findings.suggestion: Qualify the P9 rationale: blind-spot crossing is covered only on opt-in/high-stakes items; the ODP trigger should include a masking incident on a default (non-异源) item.

findings.location: proposal P7-b + Non-goals third bullet, vs intent-blueprint.md §Rich path (lines 33-45) and plan-driven-mode.md chaining-loop step 3 (line 150)
findings.evidence: P7-b anchors the seam "at Phase 0 freeze" and treats "Absent seam → name-only degrade" as the exception. But the rich path derives blueprints from bc specs: "spec `acceptance-criteria` → Blueprint AC, refined into BDD Given/When/Then" (intent-blueprint.md:37) and "Rich path: if `plan_queue.detect_producer` reports `blueprint-crafting`, seed the Phase-0 anchor from bc's spec in the `authority_chain` (derive, don't re-imagine)" (plan-driven-mode.md:150). The proposal's own Non-goal — "blueprint-crafting authoring-side changes are out of scope" — guarantees bc specs carry no seam field, so on the rich path (the path P8-a itself targets) every mini-blueprint's AC line systematically lacks a seam and the degrade becomes the norm. That is precisely the failure the proposal quotes against in P7-b: "若上游没有发生协商，守卫的前置条件从不触发，运行静默退化为'直接写代码'" (wiki test-seam §上游冻结). The proposal never says whether the Planner should synthesize seams during rich-path derivation or accept systematic mid-RED identification (P7-a's fallback).
findings.suggestion: State the rich-path seam source explicitly: either the Planner derives a seam at seeding (making the upstream anchor real), or the proposal concedes the degrade is systematic for bc-seeded plans and records that honestly.

findings.location: proposal P8-b ("Migrate: batch call-site migration by package/dir, each batch one unit, all blocked by expand") vs refactoring.md Phase 3 (lines 47-72)
findings.evidence: P8-b's expand-contract is expressed in unit/dependency terms — "each batch one unit, all blocked by expand", "Contract: ... blocked by all migrate batches" — but blocking edges between work units exist only in plan-driven mode's queue machinery (plan_queue.py `depends_on`, next-item deps check). refactoring.md Phase 3 ("Refactoring (Parallel when safe)") is a prose workflow whose only dispatch pattern is "For independent files/modules: Task(...): Refactor module A (keep tests green)" with no dependency graph and no unit concept. The proposal does not say whether a standalone wide refactor must route through plan-driven mode to obtain the blocking semantics, or how Phase 3 expresses "all blocked by expand" without queue machinery — the carve-out's core safety property (CI stays green because sequencing is enforced) has no carrier at its stated edit point.
findings.suggestion: Either state that wide refactors decompose only in plan-driven mode (P8-a's queue) with refactoring.md Phase 3 carrying a pointer, or specify how the expand→migrate→contract ordering is enforced within a plain Phase-3 run.

findings.location: proposal P8-a placement + Consistency notes rule-5 enumeration, vs feature-dev.md Phase 1 (line 33) / Phase 5
findings.evidence: P8-a lands the tracer-bullet doctrine solely in plan-driven-mode.md Phase −1 (plan interpretation), and the rule-5 enumeration lists feature-dev.md only for P7-a. But the default (non-plan-driven) feature lifecycle performs its own decomposition at feature-dev.md Phase 1 — "Break down into subtasks" (line 33) — feeding Phase 5's parallel dispatch. For a plain "implement feature X end-to-end" request, the decomposition decision point never sees the thin-slice-first doctrine; per the workspace's own rule 8 ("a file existing somewhere is not enough"), the P8 capability is unreachable where default-mode decomposition happens. The proposal scopes P8 to "plan interpretation" without stating why feature-dev's decomposition is excluded, though the borrowed article's claim is about decomposition generally.
findings.suggestion: Add the one-sentence tracer-bullet cross-ref to feature-dev.md Phase 1 (and enumerate it in rule 5), or record an explicit non-goal excluding default-mode decomposition with the reason.

findings.location: proposal P7 (a/b/c) vs fetched mattpocock docs/engineering/tdd.md §The loop, and the seam it runs at
findings.evidence: The fetched primary source (verified 2026-08-24, raw.githubusercontent.com/mattpocock/skills/main/docs/engineering/tdd.md) states the pre-agreed-seam rule as a TWO-sided mechanism: "In the full chain the seams are agreed earlier, during to-spec: '/tdd is told to only work at pre-agreed test seams, /code-review checks that only agreed-upon test seams were used.'" The proposal translates only the upstream half (P7-b freeze, P7-a consumption). P7-c's reviewer additions — tautological assertion, implementation-coupled test, no-independent-truth-source — do not include a seam-conformance check ("did the tests actually sit at the blueprint-declared seam rather than an internal helper?"). The implementation-coupled check is adjacent (breaks on internal rename) but does not verify against the DECLARED seam, so a Coder testing a different boundary than the frozen one has no review-side detection.
findings.suggestion: Add a fourth P7-c reviewer check: tests target the seam declared on the blueprint AC line (drift → finding), mirroring mattpocock's code-review half.

findings.location: proposal P7-b ("Absent seam → name-only degrade with an honest coverage note (rule 3)")
findings.evidence: "name-only degrade" is a load-bearing but undefined term: nothing in the proposal or the touched files says what is name-only, or what operationally degrades. The nearest existing pattern uses different words — intent-blueprint.md:23: "Absent mapping → the gate degrades to an **inactive coverage note** (no name comparison runs...)". An implementer cannot tell whether "name-only" refers to the AC line carrying only its name, the gate comparing names only, or something else. This also contradicts the proposal's own Consistency note: "Rule 10 terminology: one term per concept" — a new compound term is introduced without a gloss, the exact drift rule 10 forbids.
findings.suggestion: Define the degrade concretely at first use (e.g. "the AC line carries no seam field; RED identifies one and records it as a coverage note"), reusing the existing 'inactive coverage note' idiom.

findings.location: proposal P8-a per-item shape rules vs plan-driven-mode.md Phase −1 capabilities 1 and the extraction-mode table (lines 49-57)
findings.evidence: Phase −1's extraction doctrine says upstream decomposition structure is trusted: "Cursor `todos[]` frontmatter; iteration-plan tables; decomposition tables → **Latch** (structural — high confidence)" and capability 1 "**Plan-native grain.** Do NOT canonicalize grain." P8-a's new rule — "Validation question: 'what can be demoed when this item completes?' No answer → it is a horizontal slice, split it" — licenses the normalizer to second-guess and re-split exactly those latched items. The proposal states no precedence rule between a latched upstream decomposition (e.g. bc's iteration-plan Coder-L/M/E/G) and the split doctrine, leaving the normalizer to choose between two conflicting instructions at the same decision point.
findings.suggestion: State the precedence: e.g. the shape rules apply to semantically-inferred decompositions and as a checkpoint-flagged advisory on latched ones (revision channel), never a silent re-split of latched grain.

findings.location: Fix P7-b, absent-seam degrade carrier sentence
findings.evidence: Doc: "RED identifies the seam mid-phase per P7-a; the identification travels in the Coder's folded inner summary (the only free-form channel — the run-record schema has no notes field and additionalProperties: false, so no schema'd carrier exists)". The named carrier is neither free-form nor available at RED. (1) infra/scripts/loop_state.py:194-207 `summary()` is a deterministic f-string template — `f"Inner status={state.get('status')}, iteration {inner.get('iteration', 0)}/{inner.get('cap_M', DEFAULT_CAP_M)}, last_snapshot={inner.get('last_snapshot')}. Fingerprints: {fp_part}."` — composed only of status, iteration count, snapshot ref, and top-3 fingerprint counts; there is NO input by which an agent can place a seam name in it. convergent-loop.md:162 confirms: "`loop_state.py summary` emits one folded sentence from the fingerprint log + status" — an emission, not a channel. (2) Role/phase mismatch: P7-a places the identification in Phase 4 RED, whose Role is Test Engineer → solidforge:tester (feature-dev.md:74); the folded inner summary is produced by the GREEN-phase Coder (convergent-loop.md:14: "Coder (per-task subagent)... returns the final Diff + a one-sentence folded inner summary") at inner convergence — a later phase, a different agent. The degrade path's auditability claim (rule-3 honesty) rests on a carrier that cannot carry.
findings.suggestion: Pick a carrier that exists at RED: e.g. the AC→test mapping bullet's test name, a TaskCreate metadata field, or amend loop_state with an explicit seam field — or honestly state NO carrier exists and the degrade is unverifiable.

findings.location: Fix P8-b, entry-path sentence ("or a user-approved minimal expand-contract queue at the mandatory checkpoint")

With no plan @ref the mode is never entered, so no checkpoint exists at which a synthesized expand-contract queue could be user-approved. The P8-b edit set (a Phase-3 routing pointer only) adds no mode-entry rule, and the Non-goals list none either — the entry mechanism for this case is a missing step.
findings.suggestion: Either route the middle case through an explicit step (orchestrator drafts the minimal queue as a plan doc the user then @refs) or drop the middle case and state the binary: @ref → plan-driven; no plan → advisory.

findings.location: Fix P7-c, template item 3 new check (g)
findings.evidence: Doc (g): "seam conformance — do the tests sit at the seam declared on the blueprint AC line; testing a different boundary than the frozen one is a finding". findings.location: Context, first paragraph ("The wiki research verified: the concepts are classic ..., the packaging is new")
findings.evidence: Doc: "The wiki research verified: the concepts are classic (Feathers 2004, Hunt & Thomas 1999), the packaging is new." No vendored wiki page verifies the packaging's novelty: test-seam.md 来源 calls the article "概念大众化转述" and tracer-bullet.md 来源 likewise — neither says the packaging is new. And mattpocock-skills.md describes mattpocock/skills as ALREADY orchestrating the three mechanisms ("把 [[test-seam]]、[[tracer-bullet]]、[[review-axis-separation]] 三个机制编排成一条各阶段职责互不重叠的链"), with the vendored article itself saying mattpocock's workflow "就遵循上述 三位一体开发流程" (article-kasong-tdd.md, final section). Whether the packaging is in fact new is outcome-axis (not judged); the defect is attributing that verification to the wiki research when the vendored record contains no such finding.
findings.suggestion: Re-attribute "the packaging is new" to the article's own claim or mark it unverified — do not credit it to the wiki research.

findings.location: P7-a, seam-type table (Examples column)
findings.evidence: The table is introduced under "Feathers enumerates three seam types (wiki `test-seam` §定义与机制, verified):" — but the wiki section lists only the three type names with one-line mechanisms ("预处理接缝（条件编译替换）、链接接缝（链接期替换实现）、对象接缝（多态/接口替换）"). The Examples column ("Rust traits, Java interfaces, Python protocols" / "linker substitution" / "conditional compilation") appears nowhere in the wiki snapshot, and "DI" in the Mechanism column is an addition beyond 多态/接口替换. The unverified column rides a "verified" citation tag with no separate attribution — in a doc that is scrupulous about this distinction one sentence later ("The scoping-out is this proposal's own judgment, not a wiki claim").
findings.suggestion: Attribute the Examples column explicitly (own instantiation or Feathers book) so the "verified" tag covers only what the wiki carries.

findings.location: Consistency notes, rule-10 bullet ("Seam types are a 2-attribute mapping → rendered as a table")
findings.evidence: The consistency note self-describes the P7-a table as a "2-attribute mapping", but the table it points to renders three attributes — the header row is "| Seam type | Mechanism | Examples |". Minor, but the note exists precisely to document rule-10 compliance ("Prefer a table when each item has two or more attributes"), and it miscounts its own artifact.
findings.suggestion: Correct to a 3-attribute row or drop the count.

findings.location: P7-c template item 3 check (f) — verification disclosure on prior finding r7-same-2
findings.evidence: Re-verified (f) against wiki test-seam §权衡与局限 · 根缺口 and found the current text DOES carry the so-called missing half: "(wiki `test-seam` §权衡与局限 · 根缺口 — the wiki ties this gap's RESOLUTION to the 异源-oracle result-axis constraint, isomorphic to two-axis-evaluation-separation; this check is the same-family tripwire only, not the resolution)" — matching the wiki's "这与 [[two-axis-evaluation-separation]] 要求结果轴由异源 oracle 裁决的约束同构". r7-same-2's evidence premise ("(f) imports the root-gap flag but drops the wiki's isomorphism half") therefore does not match the artifact under review; dispatching its suggested fix would edit text that already exists. Naming this so the convergence loop does not act on a stale finding; no doc defect found at this location.
findings.suggestion: Re-check r7-same-2 against the current revision before sending a fix round.
